title: Cities that kept paying after a team left

rows.public_obligation: None identified: arena built 1995 with C$160M private financing (Orca Bay)
rows.notes: No public arena debt left behind found.
rows.label: c

rows.public_obligation: $52M city arena financed with $47M general-obligation bonds approved by voters in 1984; debt still outstanding in the 1990s; payoff date not found
rows.notes: Coliseum (14 yrs old at departure) demolished June 2007. City then built a ~$260-265M uptown arena (approved 2002-11-11) for the expansion Bobcats; city finance dept put total cost incl. debt at ~$430M over the building's life; 2022 added $275M more.
rows.label: c (payoff not verified)

rows.public_obligation: $65M public arena; city spent $7M to adapt it for the Grizzlies (2001); team contract barred competing use, building went dark 2004-2015 until Bass Pro lease
rows.label: c

rows.public_obligation: $200,000 renovation for Hornets lease; no debt found
rows.label: c

rows.public_obligation: 1995 renovation financed by city (city $74.5M); remaining KeyArena GO debt (Series 2002B, 2003, 2005) defeased in 2008
rows.who_paid: Paid from the team's $45M lease-break settlement, not taxpayers; rest of settlement: legal $2.8M, improvements $2.3M, other Seattle Center $3.8M, lost revenue $1.4M
rows.notes: Contingent extra $30M (tied to 2009 state renovation funding and no new team in 5 years) - payment not confirmed. Seattle Center budget later reported thin arena reserves after the Sonics left.
rows.label: c

rows.public_obligation: State-owned Meadowlands arena (NJSEA) lost tenants; projected $8.5M loss for 2015; NJSEA voted 2015-01-15 to close it. Newark had pledged $210M (airport-lease settlement money) toward the $375M Prudential Center, originally also meant for the Nets, who played there only 2010-12
rows.notes: NBA-specific share of NJSEA debt not quantified.
rows.label: c

rows.public_obligation: City loan to team (1997, ~$70M; $77M balance in 2011)
rows.who_paid: Loan owed by team to city; resolution not verified here
rows.notes: Within-city move; old arena site later donated for a medical campus (2021).
rows.label: u

rows.public_obligation: Coliseum Authority $140M lease-revenue bonds (Aug 1996) for $121M renovation; $80M refunded 2015 (taxable); final maturity 2026; debt service $5.1-10.5M/yr FY2020-26 (Moody's)
rows.who_paid: Arbitrator (2018) held the Warriors liable for the shortfall between arena net revenue and remaining debt (reported ~ $40M); upheld by Superior Court, Court of Appeal (Aug 2020); Cal. Supreme Court denied review 2020-12-09. City and county (50/50 JPA owners) remain the backstop.
rows.notes: Taxpayer exposure was limited by the arbitration win; arena lost its NBA tenant.
rows.label: c

rows.team_left: (built to attract NBA/NHL; none came; Kings had left KC in 1985)
rows.public_obligation: Arena bonds repaid from $4/day rental-car and $1.50/night hotel fees (2004 vote); ~$213M variable-rate bonds later restructured
rows.period: outstanding per KCUR list (date unclear); payoff 2040
rows.who_paid: Visitor fees; general fund tapped for the first time (~$4.2M) in FY2021-22 for repairs
rows.notes: No anchor tenant 17+ years after opening.
rows.label: c (figure date unclear)

method: select l.city, l.arena, l.team_left, l.year_left, l.public_obligation, l.amount_usd_m, l.period, l.who_paid, l.notes, l.label, coalesce((select list(s.source_id order by s.ord) from left_behind_sources s where s.city = l.city), []) as sources from left_behind l order by l.year_left, l.city
